_comment: Generated by apps/api/scripts/generate_guidance_catalogue.py from the legacy domain/species.py BAIT_DB and NATURAL_BAIT_DB. Regenerate rather than hand-edit.

baits.name: Live shrimp
baits.note: Top choice for speckled trout and versatile for many species; use under a popping cork or on bottom rigs.

seasonal_notes.note: Live shrimp are scarce at bait shops in winter; frozen shrimp or Fishbites are a reliable substitute.

baits.name: Cut mullet
baits.note: Excellent for red drum and black drum; fresh cut strips release scent and stay on the hook.

seasonal_notes.note: Fall mullet run makes fresh mullet abundant and free; stock up and freeze for year-round use.

baits.name: Menhaden (live or cut)
baits.note: Prime bait for red drum, bluefish and striped bass; live menhaden offer a distinct advantage in calm conditions.

seasonal_notes.note: Menhaden are offshore in winter; use frozen cut menhaden or substitute with cut mullet.
Menhaden schools are thick along the beach during fall; cast-net your own for the freshest bait.

baits.name: Sand fleas (mole crabs)
baits.note: Effective for whiting and pompano; dig in the swash zone for fresh fleas.

seasonal_notes.note: Sand fleas are buried deep or absent in cold months; use Fishbites Sand Flea flavor as a substitute.
Sand fleas are returning to the swash zone; dig at the water's edge as waves recede.

baits.name: Squid strips
baits.note: Durable on the hook; attracts black sea bass, whiting, and puffer fish on the East Coast, and rockfish, lingcod, and halibut on the West Coast. Available frozen year-round at any bait shop.

baits.name: Fiddler crabs
baits.note: Essential for sheepshead and tautog; use whole crabs on small strong hooks.

seasonal_notes.note: Fiddler crabs are dormant in winter burrows; check bait shops or use fresh shrimp as a substitute.
Fiddler crabs are emerging from winter burrows; trap them in marsh mud at low tide.

baits.name: Bloodworms
baits.note: Popular for whiting, black drum, spot and puffer fish; cut into small pieces for double-dropper rigs.

seasonal_notes.note: Bloodworms are a top winter bait; their scent and movement attract cold-water bottom feeders when other baits are scarce.
Bloodworms during the fall spot run are unbeatable; small pieces on #6 hooks catch spot after spot.

baits.name: Clams and crab pieces
baits.note: Best for black drum; larger pieces stay on the hook and deter small pickers. Available year-round.

baits.name: Live finger mullet
baits.note: Top producer for flounder and red drum; hook through the lips and drift slowly along the bottom.

seasonal_notes.note: Live finger mullet are hard to find in winter; try frozen mullet strips or live shrimp as alternatives.
Finger mullet are everywhere during the fall run; cast-net your own for the liveliest bait.

baits.name: Fresh shrimp pieces
baits.note: Cut shrimp on bottom rigs is a universal bait for smaller surf and pier species. Available frozen year-round.

baits.name: Live cigar minnows or threadfin
baits.note: Prime bait for king mackerel and false albacore; rig on wire leader with stinger hook.

seasonal_notes.note: Cigar minnows are not available inshore in winter; frozen are a poor substitute for kings.

baits.name: Large cut menhaden or bluefish chunks
baits.note: Heavy shark baits; use fresh, bloody chunks on wire leader for maximum scent trail. Frozen works year-round.

baits.name: Live blue runners
baits.note: Top live bait for large gamefish; catch on sabiki rigs and fish on heavy tackle.

seasonal_notes.note: Blue runners are not available inshore in winter months.

baits.name: Live menhaden (pogies)
baits.note: The king of live baits in NC; cast-net schools and fish on circle hooks for almost any large gamefish.

seasonal_notes.note: Live pogies are hard to find in winter; use frozen cut menhaden or live mullet as alternatives.
Massive menhaden schools are along the beach in fall; cast-net more than you need and freeze the rest.

baits.name: Ballyhoo (rigged or live)
baits.note: Premier offshore trolling bait; rig on wire or heavy fluorocarbon for billfish and pelagics.

seasonal_notes.note: Frozen ballyhoo are available at offshore tackle shops year-round for winter Gulf Stream trips.

baits.name: Shad darts and small jigs
baits.note: Essential tackle for spring shad runs; fish tandem rigs in current near river mouths and bridges.

seasonal_notes.note: This is THE time for shad darts; bright colors (pink, chartreuse, white) in 1/16-1/8 oz are the standard.
Off-season for shad; save these for the spring river runs.

baits.name: Live crabs (blue crab, fiddler)
baits.note: Top bait for structure-oriented species; use whole small crabs or halved blue crabs on circle hooks.

seasonal_notes.note: Crabs are dormant in cold months; use fresh shrimp or clam pieces as a substitute for structure species.

baits.name: Cut squid strips
baits.note: Durable and versatile bottom fishing bait; stays on the hook well for reef and wreck species. Frozen year-round.

baits.name: Cedar plugs and trolling feathers
baits.note: Classic offshore trolling lures for tuna; troll at 6-8 knots in clean blue water. Tackle shop staple.

baits.name: Fishbites (artificial strips)
baits.note: Scented artificial bait strips that stay on the hook forever; great substitute when live/fresh bait is unavailable.

seasonal_notes.note: Fishbites are the go-to winter bait when live options are scarce; Sand Flea and Shrimp flavors work best.

baits.name: Live or frozen anchovy
baits.note: The West Coast's all-purpose live bait; fish it under a float, freelined, or on a sliding sinker rig. Available at nearly every Southern California bait barge.

baits.name: Live sardine
baits.note: Premium West Coast live bait when anchovies are scarce; more expensive but often outfishes anchovy for bigger yellowtail and seabass.

baits.name: Ghost shrimp / mud shrimp
baits.note: Pumped from sand or mud flats at low tide; the top bait for corbina and surfperch working the wash.

baits.name: Live opelu or squid (ika)
baits.note: Classic Hawaii live-bait for ulua and papio; slow-troll or float-fish it along reef edges and channels.

baits.name: Menhaden (bunker)
baits.note: Schools visible at surface — look for diving birds

baits.name: Mullet
baits.note: Year-round; large fall runs Sept-Nov along beaches

baits.name: Sand fleas (mole crabs)
baits.note: Dig in wet sand at surf's edge during wave retreat

baits.name: Shrimp
baits.note: Peak summer/fall; run on outgoing tides at night

baits.name: Fiddler crabs
baits.note: Found in mud flats at low tide — top sheepshead bait

baits.name: Bloodworms
baits.note: Available year-round at bait shops; pricey but effective

baits.name: Cut bait (spot/croaker)
baits.note: Catch small spot/croaker on Sabiki rigs for fresh cut bait

baits.name: Finger mullet
baits.note: Cast net along shore; top live bait for predator species

baits.name: Silversides
baits.note: Tiny baitfish in surf zone — match with small spoons/jigs

baits.name: Blue crab
baits.note: Cut in half for drum/sheepshead; chicken necks to trap

baits.name: Sand crabs
baits.note: Dig at wave line for prime surfperch and corbina bait

baits.name: Mussels
baits.note: Pry from rocks at low tide — excellent all-purpose bait

baits.name: Anchovies
baits.note: Buy live or use Sabiki rig; top live bait for gamefish

baits.name: Sardines
baits.note: Available live at bait barges; great for halibut and bass

baits.name: Squid
baits.note: Market squid runs in winter; cut strips or use whole

baits.name: Ghost shrimp
baits.note: Pump from mudflats at low tide; perch and surfperch love them

baits.name: Mackerel (bait)
baits.note: Catch on Sabiki rigs at piers; cut for halibut and bass

baits.name: Grunion
baits.note: Beach spawning runs on full/new moon nights — check regulations

baits.name: Squid (ika)
baits.note: All-purpose frozen bait for papio, goatfish, and reef species

baits.name: ʻOpae (shrimp)
baits.note: Small shrimp on light tackle — deadly for papio and oio (bonefish)

baits.name: ʻOama (juvenile goatfish)
baits.note: Net in the summer shallows — premier live bait for papio (jacks)

baits.name: Halalu (juvenile akule)
baits.note: Summer/fall scad run; live-line or cut for ulua and papio

baits.name: Tako (octopus)
baits.note: Tough cut bait that stays on the hook for ulua and large reef fish

baits.name: Aku belly (cut bait)
baits.note: Oily strip bait prized for ulua slide-baiting off the rocks

baits.name: Limu (seaweed)
baits.note: Targets herbivores like manini and nenue (rudderfish)
